name: Central bank stress
summary: Markets price a Fed rate rise in December; Japan steps up warnings as the yen holds near 159.3 per dollar
state: Markets priced about a 91% chance of a Fed rate rise in December as of 11 Nov (Trading Economics). The yen stalled just short of 160 per dollar on 12 Nov as intervention risk grew (FXStreet), and on 18 Nov held near 159.3 after Finance Minister Katayama said authorities would take appropriate action when necessary and would coordinate with US counterparts (Trading Economics). No emergency inter-meeting move or confirmed intervention was found as of 19 Nov.
for_you: Rising US rates and a weak yen tend to feed through to borrowing costs, mortgage pricing and import prices. Travellers to Japan face a weak yen; Japanese warnings mean sudden currency moves are possible.
rubric_hit: Watch: G7 FX intervention threat (Japan warnings, yen ~159.3) and stagflationary rate-rise dilemma; no emergency move (Alert)

sources.title: Trading Economics — Yen weakens on Fed rate hike expectations
FXStreet — Japanese Yen decline halts a few pips shy of 160.00 as intervention risks grow

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
